author: felicepantaleo
body:
#### PR description:

This PR adds `isInTime()` to the truth-graph particles and vertices. It is true for the interactions in bunch crossing 0: the signal and the in-time pile-up. It is false for the out-of-time pile-up.

The method is on `truth::ParticleData`, `truth::VertexData`, the `truth::Particle` and `truth::Vertex` views, and the python `TruthGraphView` in `PhysicsTools/TruthInfo/python/graphTools.py`. It uses the same definition as the existing `truth::Branch::isInTime()`: `bunchCrossing() == 0`. An invalid view returns false, as for `isSignal()` and `isFromPileup()`.

`isFromPileup()` is not the opposite of `isInTime()`: an in-time pile-up particle is in time and from pile-up. The new method lets a consumer select the in-time interactions without decoding the `EncodedEventId` by hand.

The change adds inline and out-of-line member functions only. No data member changes, so there is no data-format change and no ClassVersion update.

`truth::Branch::isInTime()` returns `root().isInTime()`, so a branch and its root use one definition. Tests cover `isInTime()` on invalid particle and vertex views (false) and the python `isInTimeEventId` and `TruthGraphView.isInTime`.

#### PR validation:

- New unit test `TestInteractions::testInTime` in `PhysicsTools/TruthInfo/test/Interactions_t.cpp`: four interactions in bunch crossings 0, 0, -1 and 2, with event indices 0, 5, 0 and 3. `isInTime()` is true for the first two and false for the others, on the particles and on the vertices. `isSignal()` is true for the first one only. A default-constructed `truth::Particle` is not in time.
- The python helper gives the same result on the same four `EncodedEventId` values.
- All `PhysicsTools/TruthInfo` unit tests pass. `scram b code-format` makes no change.

@borzari fyi
title: Truth graph: add isInTime() to particles and vertices
